ai.title: Wait for ready promise before storing API key
ai.summary: CLI now awaits `this.readyPromise` before calling `handleAddApiKey`. Prevents race condition where API key storage attempt occurs before client initialization completes. Spinner displays during wait. Internal fix in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to save a new API key, it now waits for the connection to fully finish starting up before actually saving it, avoiding a situation where the key-save could be attempted too early and fail. You would notice nothing directly beyond the save completing more reliably.

ai.title: Version 1.0.203
ai.summary: Version 1.0.203. Bumped version in npm-app/package.json. Internal version increment.

eli5.text: Your installed copy of the assistant is being re-tagged to match a new release number, which bundles together several already-finished features that only take effect once you update. After updating, you get the new secure storage for your API keys, the neo-brutalist website look, and the new affiliates page for setting up referral handles. The change itself only changes the box it ships in, so you won't notice anything different until you install this update.

ai.title: Fix sign-in redirect logic for authcode
ai.summary: Updated `SignInButton` to calculate `callbackUrl` dynamically based on `pathname` and `searchParams`. If the user is on `/login` with an `auth_code`, the redirect target becomes `/onboard` preserving query params; otherwise it defaults to `/`. This ensures proper routing after OAuth completion. The change affects `web/src/components/sign-in/sign-in-button.tsx`.

eli5.text: When someone signs in to the app through the login button, the app now decides where to send them next based on exactly where they started. If you're on the /login page with an auth_code (a temporary code used during sign-in), you'll be taken to the /onboard page with that code still attached, so the onboarding flow can continue smoothly. Otherwise, you'll be sent to the home page. If you happened to look, you'd see that after clicking sign-in, the redirect behaves correctly instead of always going to the same place. This fix is live today.

ai.title: Add session logging to api-keys GET handler
ai.summary: Added console.log({ session }) to the GET handler in web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts. Import order cleaned up, moving common/db and constants before crypto/schema imports. Prettier formatting applied to logger.info call.

eli5.text: The page that loads your saved API key types now prints the current login session to the developer log when you open it, so engineers can see whether the system correctly recognizes who is signed in at that moment. You won't see anything change on the page itself; the only visible effect is extra diagnostic output that appears in the server logs whenever someone who is signed in visits that API-key listing endpoint. This applies to anyone signed into the web app and hitting the internal API-keys handler today.

ai.title: Replace getServerSession with db query in api-keys route
ai.summary: The `api-keys` route handlers now accept `authToken` in the request body and resolve the user via a direct `db.query.session` lookup, removing the dependency on `next-auth`'s `getServerSession`. The `npm-app` client was updated to include `authToken` in GET and POST payloads and to await `fetchStoredApiKeyTypes` to ensure correct sequencing. This change affects `web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts` and `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use an app to manage your API keys, the app now sends your login token directly to the server, which looks up your account in the database instead of relying on a separate session-checking tool. This affects the npm-app client and the API-key handling route. If you watched the network requests, you'd see the login token included in the request body for both fetching and storing keys, and the order of some background calls was adjusted to wait for completion before finishing. The change is live today as part of the internal tooling update.

ai.title: Add troubleshooting info to docs
ai.summary: The `getting-started.mdx` file now includes structured troubleshooting steps for installation issues. It adds a requirement for Node version 18+ with a version check command, alongside existing permission and reinstall advice. This change affects the web documentation surface only. The update uses HTML list elements with Tailwind classes for styling.

eli5.text: The help guide for new users now gives clearer steps when the assistant fails to install, including a reminder that your computer needs the right version of the underlying software and a quick way to check it. This affects anyone opening the guide to solve their own install problems, and you'd see the new checklist-style section under the troubleshooting heading.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.204
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.204 in npm-app/package.json. Package name codebuff. No feature changes.

eli5.text: The assistant's sign-in system now correctly remembers where you were trying to go and brings you back there after you log in, instead of sending you to a default page. When the system needs to check your API keys, it now talks directly to the secure storage layer instead of going through an extra session-checking step, and it quietly records these checks for troubleshooting. These fixes are live today and apply to anyone signing in or managing their API keys through the assistant.

ai.title: CLI API key detection via regex
ai.summary: Refactored CLI input handling to detect API keys using regex patterns in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Replaced simple prefix/length checks with `detectApiKey` method returning typed results (`found`, `prefix_only`, `not_found`). Handles valid keys via `handleApiKeyInput` and warns on prefix matches with incorrect length/format. Internal refactor for improved key detection logic.

eli5.text: The command-line tool got better at spotting when you paste in an API key instead of a regular command. Rather than guessing based on a rough length check, it now uses pattern-matching to find a valid key even if you accidentally include extra spaces around it, and it gives a clearer warning when what you typed starts like a key but isn't complete. If you use this tool interactively and paste a key, you'll see more accurate detection and feedback right away.

ai.title: npm-app version bump to 1.0.205
ai.summary: Version increment in `npm-app/package.json` from 1.0.204 to 1.0.205. Routine release metadata update for the codebuff package. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant can spot API keys in your command-line input using pattern matching, so it no longer needs an extra confirmation step before securely storing your credentials. This rollout bundles that improvement with a few smaller fixes, including smoother sign-in redirects, better session logging for the API keys page, and updated troubleshooting guidance in the docs.

ai.title: Unescape HTML entities in terminal commands
ai.summary: Added `transformRunTerminalCommand` to decode `&` to `&` in `run_terminal_command` parameters. Applied in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` before client tool call construction. Ensures shell commands with ampersands execute correctly.

eli5.text: You: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command that contains an ampersand (like `&`), it now works correctly instead of failing or behaving unexpectedly. The fix decodes the ampersand in the command before it's executed, so commands that rely on `&`, such as running a task in the background, behave as intended.

ai.title: Add runterminalcommand single-call rule to tools.ts
ai.summary: Added instruction 10 to backend/src/tools.ts prohibiting multiple run_terminal_command calls in a single response. This enforces sequential execution, requiring the agent to wait for tool results before invoking the next command. Scope limited to backend tool definitions.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in the terminal, it can now only send one command at a time and must wait for the result before sending the next one. This prevents it from accidentally running multiple commands at once, which could lead to confusion or errors. If you were watching, you'd see the assistant pause between each command instead of trying to do everything at once.

ai.title: Move getMessagesSubset to util/messages and apply to file search
ai.summary: The `getMessagesSubset` function was moved from `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to `backend/src/util/messages.ts` to allow reuse in file search operations. `backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts` and `backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts` now use `getMessagesSubset` with a 100k token buffer to truncate messages before sending prompts to Gemini. This change also removes the `useGPT4oInsteadOfClaude` flag from `checkNewFilesNecessary`.

eli5.text: The assistant trims earlier parts of your conversation before asking which files it needs to read, so file searches now carry a 100,000-token buffer and reuse the same message-trimming logic instead of a model flag. You won't see it directly, but file lookups stay tidier and more consistent. Live in this snapshot.

ai.title: api-keys route auth via Bearer header
ai.summary: GET /api/api-keys now extracts auth token from Authorization header instead of JSON body. Client sends Bearer token in headers, dropping body payload. Server validates prefix and splits token, returning 401 on missing header. Covers npm-app client and web api-keys route.

eli5.text: When you visit the page that shows your API keys, the app no longer sends your login token inside the message body. Instead, it puts the token in a header named "Authorization" with the word "Bearer" in front of it, which is a standard way for apps to prove identity. The server now checks for that header and refuses the request with a 401 error if it is missing or does not start with "Bearer". You would notice this only if you were building or modifying a tool that talks to this internal endpoint; regular visitors will not see any difference in what appears on screen.

ai.title: Prioritize user key for Gemini 2.5 Pro exp
ai.summary: Reorders fallback chain in `streamGemini25ProWithFallbacks` to attempt user's Gemini API key first for `gemini-2.5-pro-exp`, followed by OpenRouter, Vertex, and internal keys. Adds `gemini-2.5-pro-preview` constant and implements tiered cost calculation logic in `message-cost-tracker.ts`. Updates `common/src/constants.ts` to map agent max mode to the exp model ID.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant at the highest-cost setting with a Gemini 2.5 Pro model, it will now try your own API key first instead of shared ones. You won't see anything visually different, but your requests will draw from your own account and quota rather than shared resources. The change is live today and only affects users who have configured their own Gemini API keys.

ai.title: Use Google Generative AI SDK
ai.summary: Added `@google/generative-ai` and refactored `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-api.ts` to use official SDK types (`Content`, `Part`) instead of manual `ts-pattern` matching. Replaced `transformMessages` with `transformMessagesToGoogle` to map OpenAI messages to Google format, including explicit `safetySettings` configuration. Scope limited to backend Gemini integration.

eli5.text: The backend system that talks to Google's AI models has been updated to use Google's official toolkit instead of a custom, home-built translation layer. This means the system now passes messages to Google's AI in the exact format Google's tools expect, reducing the chance of miscommunication and making it easier to adjust safety filtering for different types of content. The change is already live for backend Gemini integration.
